name: Royal Oak Medical Devices
old_description: Royal Oak Medical stands at the forefront of precision and innovation within the medical device industry.
about:
Royal Oak Medical Devices operates an 18,000-square-foot facility in Rochester Hills, Michigan, which opened in 2013. The company is privately held; no founders are named in public materials.

The company manufactures medical implants, FDA 510(k)-cleared devices, and precision components, working with materials such as titanium, cobalt chrome, stainless steel, PEEK, and thermoplastics. Production processes include multi-axis CNC turning and milling, wire EDM, ultrasonic washing with pharma-grade water, laser marking, and proprietary surface finishing. The facility supports prototyping through full-scale production and features lights-out manufacturing and automated vision inspection.

Royal Oak Medical serves the medical device industry, providing bespoke solutions for original equipment manufacturers and developers of implantable and surgical products. Its in-house design, engineering, and consulting teams collaborate with clients from concept through regulatory submission.

The company emphasizes its quality certifications—ISO 13485:2016 with design, 21 CFR Part 820 compliance, and FDA registration—as differentiators that enable it to meet stringent regulatory requirements for implantable devices.

name: Royal Plastics Inc
old_description: With 40 years of experience in molding and tooling, we can find an answer to almost any molding problem.
about:
Royal Plastics, Inc. operates from a 46,000-square-foot facility in Brookings, South Dakota. The company was started in 1978 by Arlen and Jane Rosvold and remains family-owned; today it is held by their children, Michael Peterson and Renee Novak, with the next generation represented by Thomas Peterson as assistant vice president and production manager. The business moved into its current plant in March 1999.

As a custom injection molder of thermoplastics, Royal Plastics runs 15 molding machines ranging from 50 to 300 tons, six of which are all-electric. The shop produces parts from small gram weights up to two pounds, maintaining over 1,300 active part numbers for more than 200 customers across the United States and Canada. A full-service tool room handles mold maintenance, new mold construction, and engineering changes, while an in-house engineering team uses AutoCAD and SolidWorks for mold and part design. Prototyping is supported by a Fortus 250mc 3D printer (10×10×12 in. build envelope, ABSplus-P430 material, ±0.0095 in. accuracy). Quality control relies on a Keyence IM-6120 image dimension system (±2 µm accuracy) and a Mitutoyo QM-Height 600 gauge, backed by a dedicated maintenance program.

The company serves the window and door industry—where it has 40 years of experience—and the after-market automotive sector, among other markets. Its customer base spans OEMs and tier suppliers in both the U.S. and Canada.

Royal Plastics emphasizes a problem-solving culture (“we like problems”) and cites four guiding principles: putting the customer first, imposing no resin restrictions, maintaining dependable quality, and reducing costs. These differentiators are reinforced by on-site mold storage, stocking programs, and design assistance from concept through production.

name: Royal Switchgear, a PGC Company
old_description: Mid-Central Electric specializes in manufacturing medium-voltage, oil-filled ‘Fixed Load’ transformers. Their transformers feature the industry’s most compact tanks and lightest weight, ensuring optimal aesthetics and easy installation.
about:
Royal Switchgear Manufacturing Company has operated from Bessemer, Alabama since its founding in 1914. The business is now a brand within Power Grid Components Inc. (PGC), a holding company that also includes Allied Bolt, Elliott, ITEC, Meister, Mid‑Central, Newell, Vizimax and the affiliated company Blackstone.

The company produces a full line of group‑operated and hookstick disconnect switches, utility‑specific designs and substation power connectors. Engineering and testing are performed in‑house, with an emphasis on customizing equipment to meet unique project requirements.

Royal Switchgear serves the electric power industry, supplying utilities, industrial operators, municipalities and contractors. Its products are deployed in power distribution networks where minimizing downtime and reducing maintenance costs are critical.

The company says its differentiation lies in rigorous testing, precise engineering and tailored solutions for demanding environments. By focusing on customization and responsive service, Royal aims to help clients achieve a more reliable and efficient grid.

name: Rudolph Foods Co
old_description: Located 31 miles northeast of Atlanta in Lawrenceville, Georgia, this 38,000 square foot facility is capable of producing 10 million pounds of pork rinds per year. Since 1994, the Atlanta facility has linked Rudolph Foods to the south. Save Energy Now Leader Our Lawrenceville facility was recently recognized by the U.S. Department of Energy as a 2010 Energy Saver. An Energy Saver is qualified as a facility that has achieved more than 75,000 MMBtu total energy savings or more than 7.5% total energy savings.
about:
Rudolph Foods Co is headquartered in Lima, Ohio, a city known as the "Pork Rind Capital of the World." The business remains family-owned, with the Rudolph family's original recipe—credited to Mary Rudolph—still at the core of its product line. The Lima campus houses corporate offices, a main pellet production facility, and a packaging plant. The company extended its footprint to the Southeast in 1994 with a 38,000-square-foot facility in Lawrenceville, Georgia, and to the Southwest in 2003 with a packaging operation in Dallas, Texas capable of 15 million pounds annually. Rudolph Foods acquired Whitefeather Foods, a Wapakoneta, Ohio pork rind maker founded in 1984, in 2000, and later added Lee's Pig Skins in New Hebron, Mississippi.

The company manufactures pork rinds and cracklins through pellet production and packaging processes. Its Lawrenceville plant produces up to 10 million pounds per year, while the Dallas facility handles up to 15 million pounds. Additional production sites in Wapakoneta, New Hebron, and Beaumont, California, along with international locations in Brazil, Mexico, and Denmark, support a multi-plant network. The firm also offers pellet production and packaging services to customers under its "Packaging / Pellet Customer Service" capability.

Rudolph Foods serves the snack food industry, supplying pork rind products to retail and foodservice channels. The company highlights its family recipe and consistent quality as key differentiators. In 2010, the Lawrenceville facility earned the U.S. Department of Energy's Energy Saver recognition for achieving more than 75,000 MMBtu in total energy savings.

name: Rural Manufacturing Co.
old_description: because we use them with our own livestock and farming operations.
about:
Rural Manufacturing Co. has been based in Freeman, South Dakota, since 1976, when the company moved from its original site on the Hofer family farm. The business was founded in 1968 by Vernon P. Hofer and Joe Danny Hofer, who began by building hog farrowing crates for their own operation. It remains family owned and operated, with the next generation now involved in daily management.

The company manufactures a full line of livestock equipment under its PRO SERIES brand, including portable chute side crowding tubs, alleys, and wheel corrals. Production takes place at the Freeman facility, where the firm also offers custom manufacturing services for other businesses. In addition to its own products, Rural Manufacturing acts as a dealer for more than 30 livestock equipment brands and supplies AG LEADER and OUTBACK GUIDANCE precision GPS systems for tractor guidance, mapping, and precision spraying.

Customers range from cow-calf operators to large feedlots; the portable wheel corral, for example, is rated for 60 cow/calf pairs or 140 head at 850 pounds. The company serves the broader agriculture sector, including crop producers adopting precision guidance technology. Thousands of buyers purchase directly through the Freeman location, the online store, or the FOR-MOST Livestock Equipment dealer network.

Rural Manufacturing emphasizes that its team uses the equipment on their own farms, which informs product design and durability. The company also highlights a large in-stock inventory, same pricing online and in store with free shipping on many items, and secure checkout via Square or PayPal.

name: Rushton Sheet Metal
old_description: We offer a wide variety of Exterior Solutions and Custom Fabrication Options
about:
Rushton Sheet Metal is a custom metal fabrication and installation company based in Iowa City, Iowa. Founded in 2008 as a family-owned business by Rob and Eric Rushton, the company grew from a background in the roofing industry, with craftsmanship and hard work as its founding principles.

The shop provides custom sheet metal fabrication, architectural sheet metal installation, ACM/MCM panel fabrication and installation, commercial and residential roofing (flat and sloped), standing seam roofing, flush panel soffit/siding systems, gutters, downspouts, wall caps, coping, fascia, and custom chimney caps. They work with metals including ACM panels, aluminum, bronze, carbon steel, copper, and stainless steel. The company operates from a facility Bay 4, though facility size and headcount are not specified. They hold certifications as a Red Shield Contractor by Firestone Building Products, Petersen Aluminum Corporation, Morin Corporation, and Edge certified installers by Metal Design Systems, plus certified Nichiha and James Hardie installers.

Rushton Sheet Metal serves commercial and residential customers across the Corridor area, including homeowners, architects, property management companies, and general contractors. Projects span commercial roofing and exterior solutions, building envelope systems, and residential siding and roofing.

The company emphasizes its uncompromising demand for quality and proven track record of excellent workmanship, aiming to be the preferred sheet metal contractor in the region. The founders' combined decades of experience in fabrication, production, and roofing underpin its capability to handle projects of any size.

name: S.A.R. METAL PRODUCTS
old_description: At our precision metal brake bending services, we combine our expertise, state-of-the-art equipment, and dedication to quality to provide exceptional bending solutions. Whether you require sheet metal bending, plate bending, or custom fabrication, our team is ready to deliver accurate, precise, and reliable results.
about:
S.A.R. Metal Products operates from a facility on Philadelphia Road in Baltimore, Maryland. The family-owned sheet metal fabrication shop was established in 1985 and has served the Mid-Atlantic region for more than 40 years.

The company specializes in custom metal fabrication with a focus on electrical enclosures — including BGE service entrance troughs, NEMA 1 and NEMA 3R cabinets, UL-approved CT cabinets, and custom junction boxes — as well as stainless steel countertops, corner guards, and custom flashing for construction. Its shop runs welding (TIG, MIG, stick), precision brake bending for sheet and plate, laser, plasma, and waterjet cutting, shearing, and CNC punch press operations for hole punching, forming, embossing, notching, and slitting. The team also handles prototyping, small-batch runs, and production parts such as brackets, clips, and light mounts. The company reports more than 10,000 completed projects and 200-plus clients.

Customers include electrical contractors, general contractors, plumbers, and commercial window companies across Maryland and surrounding states. The fabrication work supports electrical infrastructure, commercial construction, and building envelope projects.

The owners say the business was built on pride in metalworking skill, attention to detail, and quality customer service, aiming to surpass client expectations on every job.

name: SCI Electronics Inc
old_description: From AV design in the executive boardroom to digital signage indoors and out, we have the expertise to get the job done.
about:
Founded in 1976 in Greenville, South Carolina, SCI Electronics Inc has operated as a technology solutions provider for over five decades. The privately held company began as a specialist in communications infrastructure and has expanded its scope to cover a full spectrum of audio-visual, security, and cabling services.

The firm designs and installs integrated systems for commercial and institutional clients. Its service portfolio includes audio-visual design and digital signage deployment, electronic access control and CCTV video surveillance, voice and data cabling for both inside-plant and outside-plant applications, distributed audio and paging systems, and mass notification solutions. SCI Electronics coordinates the entire project lifecycle, from initial needs analysis through implementation and ongoing support.

The company works with businesses across a wide range of local and national industries, delivering customized technology infrastructure for communications, security, and paging needs.

SCI Electronics differentiates itself through a consultative methodology: it analyzes each client's technology requirements, coordinates design and implementation, and delivers a comprehensive master plan that keeps business objectives at the forefront. The company states that this approach ensures a solution crafted to exceed expectations for craftsmanship and performance.

name: SD Concept Engineering
old_description: Since 1995, SD Concepts has been fabricating custom boost kits for a wide variety of GM, Ford and Mopar vehicles.
about:
SD Concept Engineering, Inc. (SDCE) was founded in 1995 in East Providence, Rhode Island. The company began as SD Concepts, fabricating custom boost kits for GM, Ford, and Mopar vehicles, and has since grown into a full-service high-performance engine and vehicle builder.

Today, SDCE operates a machine shop equipped with manual Bridgeport mills, a manual lathe, and a CNC milling machine, alongside a dedicated engine assembly room. Its core services include engine building, forced induction systems, engine and chassis dyno tuning, custom tubing and exhaust fabrication, fueling, wiring, cooling, and suspension work. The company also produces a line of high-performance parts under the Air/Fuel Innovations (AFI) brand, developed from over 30 years of product development.

SDCE serves the automotive performance aftermarket, focusing on owners and builders of Mopar, GM, and Ford cars and trucks. Customers range from individual enthusiasts seeking custom engine builds or boost kits to shops requiring dyno tuning and fabrication services. Projects have included custom intake manifolds, twin-turbo setups for Dakota trucks, and complete engine assemblies for vehicles such as AMC and Ford Mod motors.

The company emphasizes its decades of hands-on experience as a differentiator, noting that its AFI product line is the culmination of over 30 years of innovation from its own vehicle builds. In-house machining, assembly, and dyno capabilities allow SDCE to control quality from raw fabrication to final tuning.
